subject: Request: Autopin + Failover Safety Harness for SummitPay rollout
messages:
From: Amelia Rossi <amelia.rossi@summitpay.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Cc: SummitPay SRE <sre@summitpay.com>
Date: 2028-05-22T09:07:00-07:00
Subject: Redwood rollout safety: can we get autopin + automatic fallback in the SLA?

Hi Jordan,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — SummitPay is excited about the latency profile and cost numbers. We are moving this into a limited prod rollout for our authorization flow (card tokenization calls) the week of June 5.

Before we kick off, our legal/SRE teams need explicit language (and an operational plan) for how Redwood will behave if a new model variant degrades our latency or error budget during an A/B or canary rollout. Specifically:

- We need an automatic failback/pin mechanism that can revert traffic to the previously stable model without manual intervention.
- We'd like a minimum pin hold window (e.g., 30 minutes) plus an option to manually override.
- Clarification on whether this behavior is covered under the hosted SLA or requires a Dedicated commitment.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can support an "autopin + failover safety harness" for this deployment and, if so, what the activation thresholds and operational constraints would be? If you prefer, happy to jump on a quick call with product/ops.

Attached is our internal SLO matrix for the authorization route (p95 <= 90ms, availability 99.98%).

Best,
Amelia
Senior Product Ops, SummitPay

Attachment: summitpay-slo-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet stub)

Hi Amelia — thanks for the clear ask and for sharing the SLOs. Short answer: yes, we can provide an automated rollback/pinning safety harness as part of the rollout, but there are a few operational points to align on (and one case where dedicated capacity changes the commitment). Looping in Lauren (product) and Marcus (runtime) to confirm the concrete thresholds and any contractual language required.

Proposed next steps:
1) Lauren & Marcus to propose a canary schedule + telemetry gates matching your p95/availability constraints.
2) We document an "autopin" policy: if error rate or p95 exceed thresholds for X minutes across the canary cohort, the system auto-pins to the last-known-good model variant and routes traffic back.
3) We codify the pin hold window (default 30m) and provide a manual override for your SREs.
4) If you need SLA-backed uptime guarantees tied to automatic fallback, we may need to scope Dedicated capacity or an SLA addendum — Lauren will clarify.

I'll hold a 30-minute slot tomorrow 11am PT for a quick sync if that works for you./Jordan

— Jordan Blake
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Redwood rollout safety: can we get autopin + automatic fallback in the SLA?

Thanks for the loop, Jordan — and hi Amelia. Below is a pragmatic canary + autopin proposal we use for latency-sensitive routes; I tailored thresholds to SummitPay's p95 target you shared.

Canary plan (recommended):
- Stage: 3-step progressive canary (1% -> 10% -> 30%) over 2 hours.
- Observation windows: 10 minutes per step for telemetry; require 2 consecutive windows to trigger fail/back.
- Telemetry gates (what we evaluate): p95 latency, 5xx error rate, and token generation timeout counts.

Autopin/failover rules:
- If p95 latency degrades by >20% above baseline AND 5xxs increase by >0.1% within the observation windows, the runtime automatically pins back to the previous variant.
- Autopin is initiated by the routing layer and completes within <30s; redispatch to pinned variant is immediate after pin.
- Pin hold window: default 30 minutes. During that window traffic remains on the pinned variant while we diagnose.
- Manual override: authorized SummitPay SREs (list to be provided) can lift the pin and re-run a canary.

SLA/contract considerations:
- For hosted customers on pay-as-you-go, autopin provides operational safety but is not sufficient alone for SLA uptime guarantees. For SLA-backed uptime tied to automatic fallback we require a Dedicated capacity enrollment or a written SLA addendum that specifies latency SLOs and incident handling.
- We can include the autopin policy in a mutual action plan and add a contractual clause specifying pin behavior and hold windows.

Attachments: proposed-rollout-diagram.png (visual of traffic split timeline). I've attached a sample SLO-to-trigger mapping (summitpay-slo-matrix.xlsx) with threshold examples.

Let me know if the thresholds above sound reasonable and whether SummitPay requires shorter windows or different percent steps. Happy to adjust.

— Lauren Bishop
Director, Product Management, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Redwood rollout safety: can we get autopin + automatic fallback in the SLA?

Adding a couple of runtime and ops constraints so expectations are clear:

- KV cache warming: when splitting traffic to a new variant, the first million tokens will be cold for that variant; some latency increase is expected in the first 5–15 minutes depending on request patterns. The autopin thresholds should account for predictable start-up skew.
- Prefix caching & reuse: we can pre-warm the canary variant for a specified customer prefix set if SummitPay can provide representative keys ahead of the rollout. This reduces cold-start variance.
- Fallback options: automatic pin to the previous variant is the primary safety harness. As a secondary option we can route to a quantized-lower-precision variant with consistently lower latency (but potentially lower quality) — this requires an explicit traffic policy and impacts billing rate.
- Billing/commit impact: Guaranteed SLA credit for availability during fallback is only offered when running on Dedicated capacity (we need the capacity isolation to promise credits). If SummitPay proceeds Hosted-only, we will operate the autopin safety harness but SLA credits will not apply.

I'll be available on the call. If you want, we can pre-stage a warm instance in us-west during the night before the rollout to minimize startup noise.

— Marcus Lin
Senior Runtime Engineer, Redwood Inference
